insight_capabilities.routing_note: Contract 1.25. `routing` (#411) answers the same shape of question the six before it answer -- can this Orchestrator report the **Routed pair** one unit of work runs on? -- so it is per-distribution rather than run-scoped: a Run that pins `--model` does not go silent, its Pickups publish the resolution with a `defaulted_explicit_override` source, and two Runs of one binary therefore cannot differ. A port that resolves no pair declares it `false` rather than omitting it, because a Dashboard that cannot tell `this Orchestrator never routes` from `no Pickup has resolved a pair yet` shows a Route column that reads as pending forever.

run_scoped.note: Rate-card availability (#331, ADR-0026) is a fact about one Run rather than about a distribution: it says whether THIS Run reached the harness's live model listing, and two Runs of one binary can differ. It is therefore declared alongside `names` in the Run-start Insight manifest but is not one of them -- accepted from any producer, required of none. An Orchestrator that declares it publishes the resolved card under `payload_key` on `wrapper.run.start`, keyed by the harness's own model id, or `null` when it resolved none. The card is provenance, not arithmetic: nothing derives a figure from it, so an absent card never costs a figure and Cost stays a separate declaration. Prices are denominated in AI Credits per batch of `batch_size` tokens and are recorded as published -- never flattened to a single rate, because the cache prices dominate an agent loop and a card recorded lossily is not a record of what a Run was billed under. All three Orchestrators declare it (#334); `never_resolved_by` names the ports whose answer is `false` on every Run, because they subscribe to no SDK event stream and read no model listing. Those ports still declare it rather than omit it: an omitted key would leave a Dashboard unable to tell `this Orchestrator cannot report a rate` from `this Run's prices failed to load`, which is the collapse the separate declaration exists to end. A port in `never_resolved_by` fetches nothing and holds no price data -- it publishes `null` under `payload_key`.

meaning.parallel_mode: The Orchestrator can fill more than one Lane at a time.
meaning.rolling_dispatch: It refills Lanes continuously toward the Lane cap instead of grouping them behind a barrier.
meaning.integration_backlog: It admits finished Lane branches to a bounded Integration backlog and applies Integration backpressure when that backlog is full.
meaning.adaptive_lane_limit: Its Effective Lane limit contracts and expands against Pressure signals below the immutable Lane cap.
meaning.contribution_events: It emits the Lane-contribution lifecycle Event stream pinned by contribution_identity and rolling_stream_cases.

parallel_capabilities.unsupported: An Orchestrator that declares parallel_mode false MUST declare every other parallel capability false, and MUST refuse a requested Lane cap above 1 at preflight, naming the capability and the distribution. Accepting the request and running serially is the obscure failure this manifest exists to prevent.

execution_hosts.meaning: Execution-host placement relative to the Orchestrator. A list is additive so a future host does not add a boolean to every Runner-family manifest.
execution_hosts.unsupported: A requested identifier that the distribution does not declare MUST be refused at preflight, naming execution_hosts, the distribution, and the setting the operator can change.

execution_host.note: Contract 2.2. Python announces the one Execution host selected for a rolling Run on wrapper.run.start and stamps its placement on every wrapper.contribution.start, including local. The isolation grade is Run-scoped and never repeated on a contribution. Shell and PowerShell emit neither Execution-host payload because they emit no contribution lifecycle records. An absent declaration or stamp is an old trace's unknown, never an inferred local placement.

wrapper.run.start.readback_note: Contract 1.24. The Run readback section 14 obliges of an Orchestrator that routes, published on the Run's own start record rather than on an Event of its own. Every field is optional-when-present: a port that routes nothing emits Run start exactly as before and stays conforming, and a consumer reads their absence as 'this Runner does not route'. The PRODUCER is unconditional -- a Run that configured nothing publishes the readback describing exactly that, because the Run that puzzles an operator is the one where nothing they wrote appeared to take effect.
wrapper.run.start.readback_keys_not_a_count: routes carries the keys THEMSELVES, never a count of them. No validator for the [routing] table can exist -- its keys are the operator's vocabulary and its pairs are the vendor's -- so reading back what the kit parsed is the only validation available anywhere, and a count reveals neither a misspelling nor a half-filled table. unconfigured_task_type_keys is the other half: the taxonomy members no entry names. Under unsuppressed `dynamic` they await Dynamic Pickup, not the Default pair; an explicit run-wide model/effort override remains authoritative. Under `unselected` or `static` they use the Default pair.
wrapper.run.start.readback_two_efforts: Under `unselected`, effort is the GATED effort -- what would actually be sent -- and configured_effort is what Config supplied. Both travel because a readback carrying only the gated value reports the outcome and loses the request, and the request is the half an operator can correct. gate_warnings is the legacy verdict, drawn from the same vocabulary wrapper.pickup.bound's gate_warnings carries, including for the escalation rung. Under `static` or `dynamic`, retained Static routes and explicit escalation are echoed unchanged; live preflight and Pickup validate them instead of the offline roster.
wrapper.run.start.readback_route_policy: Contract 2.8. route_policy names the Route policy this Run selected (ADR-0057): `unselected` -- the default, preserving historical behaviour -- `static`, or opt-in `dynamic`. It travels because under either selected policy the hardcoded roster is not the authority and every configured pair above is published UNGATED, which is otherwise indistinguishable from a set of pairs that merely passed the gate. A consumer MUST NOT read an empty gate_warnings under `static` or `dynamic` as `the roster approved this`; it means the roster was not asked. An absent fixed escalation rung under `dynamic` does not forbid permitted outcome-aware reselection. A consumer MUST NOT treat an unrecognised policy name as `unselected`: a Runner that names a policy this consumer does not know is describing a Run whose routing it cannot explain.
wrapper.run.start.readback_roster_divergence: roster_diverged is THREE-valued: true, false, or null for an unreadable harness_version. Reasoning-effort capability is a table hardcoded in the Copilot CLI's own bundle, so the roster is a function of CLI version (ADR-0019) and a Run gating against one version while spawning another has been checking its pairs against a description of some other binary. null is 'nobody knows' and a consumer MUST NOT read it as agreement.

wrapper.stop.requested.draining: The observed count of contributions still in flight. A serial Run reports 0, never null.
wrapper.stop.requested.emitted: Once per Wind-down latch transition. drain stops refill and new work while started work drains; cancel requests cancellation only of active agent sessions and never interrupts publication.

wrapper.stop.lifted.draining: The observed count of contributions still in flight when success clears the Abandonment guard drain. strike_limit remains readable for historical traces.

wrapper.iteration.end.billing: The harness's reported billing, added additively. An Orchestrator that observes it reports it; one that cannot omits the keys entirely or reports them null. Null is unknown, never a zero that would read as free work, and never an estimate recomputed from tokens. cache_read and cache_write are components of tokens_in, not figures beside it: summing them into a token total double-counts.
wrapper.iteration.end.retirement: cost_usd was the list-price estimate, computed by git-loopy from a price table it hand-maintained. The table is deleted (#330) and Cost is the AI Credits the harness reported billing (ADR-0026), so no producer derives the field any more. It is retired rather than repurposed: a consumer must never read Credits out of a key whose name says dollars. Still accepted, not forbidden, because a port that has not yet dropped it is emitting a null it can honestly report; a consumer must ignore it.

wrapper.skill_policy.resolved.redacted: Skill identity is the canonical name: no absolute path, home directory, exposure directory, or Skill content may appear.

wrapper.pool.refreshed.emitted: Only for a complete successful shallow snapshot. An incomplete pagination, an unresolved candidate, or a failed refresh emits nothing and cannot establish emptiness.
wrapper.pool.refreshed.order: Source order, as read. The membership list is not re-sorted.

wrapper.pool.excluded.emitted: Once per ready-for-agent candidate the AFK-ready discriminator rejected, in source order, before the wrapper.afk_ready.collected it explains. A candidate the source could not read is not an exclusion: it was never discriminated against.
wrapper.pool.excluded.scope: Run-scoped, not contribution-scoped. It names work that never became a Lane contribution, so it carries the collecting Iteration's iter and no contribution identity.

wrapper.pickup.bound.routing_note: Contract 1.21. The Routing resolution section 14 reaches at this Pickup, carried on the Pickup rather than on an Event of its own: the pair resolves AT this instant, for THIS key, so a second record would be one Pickup described twice with the same cardinality. Every field is optional-when-present, so a Runner that resolves no Routed pair emits the binding exactly as before and stays conforming; a consumer reads their absence as 'this Runner does not route', never as a route it failed to report.
wrapper.pickup.bound.routing_nullable: model and effort are nullable, and a null is a VALUE rather than an absence: the backend chooses. For effort the gate warning beside it is the whole difference between an operator who asked for nothing and one whose effort was dropped, which is why gate_warnings travels instead of being consumed inside the resolver.
wrapper.pickup.bound.routing_vocabulary: model and effort are the family's existing routed-pair words — the same two wrapper.contribution.end's summary carries — so one reader reads both. routing_source is spelled in full because this payload's own reason already answers 'why' in the unrelated Pickup vocabulary (order / priority / pin), and one record cannot carry two differently-scoped answers to one word.
wrapper.pickup.bound.emitted: Once per Pickup that bound an issue, before the unit of work's agent session starts — a serial Iteration and a Lane alike, because ADR-0032 gave every unit of work a Pickup. A walk that bound nothing emits its skips and no binding.
wrapper.pickup.bound.position: The bound candidate's 1-based place in the selection order it was chosen from; considered is the length of that order. Both are required together: position 1 alone cannot tell 'the runner took the oldest' from 'the runner took the only one left', which is the question this Event exists to answer.
wrapper.pickup.bound.reason_note: pin is declared here ahead of its producer. #396 owns git-loopy run --issue N and is the only thing that may emit it; a reader that learns the value only when a stream first carries it renders an operator's first pin as an unknown string.
wrapper.pickup.bound.scope: Run-scoped, not contribution-scoped. A Pickup precedes the work it binds, so a Lane's contribution_id has not been minted yet and there is nothing but the Run to attribute it to.

wrapper.routing.resolved.emitted: Once per issue whose route was elected from live evidence -- contract 14.4's Dynamic route -- immediately BEFORE the wrapper.pickup.bound that publishes it, and therefore before the work session opens. A Run under any other Route policy emits it never; a Static route under the dynamic policy emits it never either, because the operator's own instruction was not elected from evidence and has nothing to record. A permitted later attempt on the same issue elects again and records again, so an issue the Attempt lifecycle retried carries one of these per dynamic Pickup rather than one per Run.
wrapper.routing.resolved.ordering: The one property worth pinning: provenance written after the session starts is provenance that is missing exactly when the Run died mid-decision. A consumer that sees wrapper.pickup.bound with routing_source dynamic and no preceding wrapper.routing.resolved is reading a broken Runner, not an optional record.
wrapper.routing.resolved.provenance_note: Contract 14.4. This is the local decision record the Dynamic route owes, and it is a separate Event rather than more fields on the Pickup because it answers a different question with a different cardinality: the Pickup says which pair the session runs on, this says which evidence elected it, what that evidence cost, and when each live source was read. A Runner that does not implement the Dynamic route never emits it and stays conforming.
wrapper.routing.resolved.distinguish_forecast_from_measurement: public_output_tokens_per_second is the leaderboard's published inference speed for the benchmarked model. It is NOT a measurement of how long this issue took under Copilot, and a consumer MUST NOT render it as one. A missing measurement travels as null, never as zero.
wrapper.routing.resolved.nullable: effort, measurement_at, benchmark_version and conditions are nullable, and a null is an explicit unknown the source did not publish rather than a field the Runner forgot. repeat_justification is nullable on the same terms and means the election needed none. reused_proposal_id, reused_validated_at and superseded_proposal_id are nullable and mean, respectively, that nothing was reused and that nothing was superseded.
wrapper.routing.resolved.later_attempts: Contract 14.4, ADR-0057. lifecycle_position and attempt name WHERE the issue sits and model/effort/context_tier name WHAT it will run on; a Runner MUST report them separately, because a reassessed retry that re-elects the same configuration is otherwise indistinguishable from a first election. attempt is this issue's session ordinal in this Run, including earlier Static and advancing sessions, and starts at 1. A routing refusal does not increment it. prior_attempts is the bounded evidence the election was told -- oldest first, carrying model, effort, context_tier, outcome, detail and capability_evidence -- and is an EMPTY LIST on a first attempt, never null and never omitted. Retain earlier capability failures before recent advances when bounding history; omitted rows still count toward the ordinal and input identity. A Runner MUST NOT derive lifecycle position from that ordinal or the list length: an attempt that advanced its issue without closing it reaches no ending and spends no lifecycle attempt.
wrapper.routing.resolved.reuse: Contract 14.4, ADR-0057, issue #565. routing_reuse says HOW this route was arrived at, and is one of exactly two literals. `elected` means a Route selector was called and billed for it. `revalidated` means a decision this clone's own earlier Run already recorded was re-checked against freshly read evidence and eligibility and reused WITHOUT a selector call, so selector_attempts is 0 and routing_credits is "0". A revalidated record MUST carry reused_proposal_id and reused_validated_at naming the ORIGINAL decision -- the election a selector was actually paid for -- and never the intermediate revalidation it was read back from, so a chain of reuse stays one hop deep and survives the original's log ageing out. Both are null on an elected record; superseded_proposal_id instead names a recorded decision that stopped validating and was replaced by a fresh election. relevant_input_identity is the opaque digest of the issue/context, policy, capability, evidence and attempt-history inputs the decision was made under, and equality of that digest is what a later Run checks: a Runner MUST NOT let anything routing itself writes -- this record, its timestamps, a Route projection comment, an owned Route label -- reach that digest, or reuse invalidates itself every Run. Reuse is DERIVED state read back from canonical local event history, so a Runner MUST NOT treat a tracker comment or a Route label as reuse authority, MUST NOT let a reused record authorize work or take a Lease on its own, and MUST still let a Static or run-wide route take precedence over it. A record written before reuse existed carries none of these keys, and a consumer MUST replay it as an unknown rather than as an election.
wrapper.routing.resolved.scope: Run-scoped, for the same reason wrapper.pickup.bound is: the route is elected before the work it routes, so no contribution identity exists yet.

wrapper.routing.delivery.emitted: After a final wrapper.pickup.bound has been durably recorded, once for each attempted observational tracker projection and retry. Delivery never selects, validates, or pins a Routed pair.
wrapper.routing.delivery.scope: Run-scoped. A delivery is attributed to the final Pickup it projects and is not contribution-scoped because it precedes the Agent session.

wrapper.routing.prepared.provenance_note: New proposals retain the selector configuration, source identity and model association, fresh retrieval timestamps and available measurement metadata. Historical records may omit these fields. A null measurement date, version or condition is unknown, never the retrieval date. Cancellation is an unavailable outcome with explicit detail and current routing usage, including any reported in-flight overshoot. All preparation tasks finish or are cancelled before wrapper.run.end. A Pickup never waits for unrelated tail preparation.
wrapper.routing.prepared.emitted: Once per eligible Pool candidate a running Runner prepared a Routing proposal for, ahead of the Pickup that may later bind it -- contract 14.6's Routing preparation. A Run under any other Route policy emits it never, and a Runner that prepares nothing stays conforming by emitting nothing.
wrapper.routing.prepared.ordering: Preparation records precede the wrapper.routing.resolved and wrapper.pickup.bound of the issue they describe, when that issue is picked up at all. Many are never followed by either: preparing an issue is not a claim that it will be worked.
wrapper.routing.prepared.not_a_binding: Contract 14.6, ADR-0057, issue #566. This record is NONBINDING and a consumer MUST NOT render it as a Routing resolution. It does not bind a Routed pair, does not open or alter an Agent session, does not take a Lease, does not reserve or reorder a candidate, and does not establish that the issue is admissible. The route a session actually runs on is ALWAYS the one on wrapper.pickup.bound, which is resolved by a Pickup that re-reads the live sources for itself; where the two disagree the Pickup is right and the proposal was superseded. A consumer MUST NOT read the presence or absence of these records as evidence about whether the Pool is empty.
wrapper.routing.prepared.state: state says what preparation reached and is one of exactly four literals. `proposed` means a Route selector was called and a nonbinding proposal is waiting for this issue's Pickup; model, effort and context_tier carry what it proposed and proposal_id names it. `static` means an operator's own Static route applies, so no selector call was bought. `reusable` means a decision an earlier Run recorded is available for the Pickup to revalidate; changed inputs may still require another selector call within the remaining limits. `unavailable` means routing could not propose, reason names why, and the Pickup still decides for itself -- an unavailable preparation is NOT a refusal of the issue. model, effort, context_tier, proposal_id, summary, prepared_at and valid_until are null on every state but `proposed`.
wrapper.routing.prepared.bounds: A Runner MUST bound preparation by the operator's configured Route selector concurrency and per-Run routing-credit allowance, MUST prepare the next Pickup's candidate before any speculative one, and MUST NOT prepare a candidate that is Blocked, has unresolved Readiness, has been defeated by the Attempt lifecycle, or could not be read -- none of those may cost a classifier or selector call. Once the allowance or the assessment deadline is exhausted a Runner MUST stop preparing for the rest of the Run rather than re-refusing per candidate.
wrapper.routing.prepared.scope: Run-scoped, for the same reason wrapper.routing.resolved is: preparation precedes the work it might route, so no contribution identity exists yet.

wrapper.pickup.skipped.emitted: Once per candidate a Pickup passed over, in order, before the wrapper.pickup.bound that ended the walk. Selection never blocks on a human (Wrapper contract section 7), so a candidate that cannot be taken is skipped rather than raised — and the skip is a record rather than a log line because the starvation ADR-0032 fixes was invisible precisely for want of one.
wrapper.pickup.skipped.reason_note: Open text, unlike wrapper.pool.excluded's closed set. A refusal originates in whatever admission the port applies — a routing refusal names the label it could not resolve — and closing the vocabulary would force every future admission to pick from a list written before it existed.
wrapper.pickup.skipped.scope: Run-scoped, for the same reason wrapper.pickup.bound is.

wrapper.release.advanced.emitted: After a successful Release-line commit for a closed Bump-class issue. semver:none and failed advances emit nothing.

wrapper.contribution.end.emitted: The authoritative finalized Parallel row and Strike transition. A publication that has not yet verified its closure is not a contribution end.
wrapper.contribution.end.counted_once: Lane-work and recovery Consumption and commits appear exactly once, in the originating contribution. Runner Checkpoint commits are excluded from the commit total.
wrapper.contribution.end.retirement: Retired on the same terms as wrapper.iteration.end's: the list-price estimate is deleted (#330), and Credits are never read out of a dollar-named key.

wrapper.concurrency.changed.emitted: Only for an authoritative effective-limit transition, never per observation. The configured Lane cap is immutable for the Run.
wrapper.concurrency.changed.unavailable: A signal the Run cannot observe is null, never an estimated or zero value.

wrapper.serial.requested.emitted: When refill stops, not when the serial turn is finally granted. Everything in flight drains first, and an iteration cap can end the Run before the grant, so a consumer that waits for the grant may never learn the serial half of the Pool existed.
wrapper.serial.requested.serial_required: How many serial-required items the peek that latched this saw. Null when nothing counted them: only the driver's own Pool peek can, and it is skipped once demand is latched. Never 0 — a latch with nothing behind it cannot happen.

wrapper.parallel.serial_fallback.emitted: Once per serial Iteration a Parallel-mode Run works because it found no eligible Parallel-safe candidate, immediately before the Iteration it explains. A serial turn granted while eligible Lane work remains is interleaving, not a fallback, and emits nothing. A Run that did not request Parallel mode never emits it.
wrapper.parallel.serial_fallback.scope: Run-scoped, not contribution-scoped. It names the absence of Lane work, so it carries no contribution identity.
wrapper.parallel.serial_fallback.reported: The reason MUST reach the operator's own output, not only the Event stream: the operator is the only one who can apply parallel-safe.
wrapper.parallel.serial_fallback.eligible: Always 0 when emitted. Carried explicitly because 'it found zero eligible Parallel-safe issues' is the report.

wrapper.parallel.degraded.emitted: Exactly once per Run, immediately after the wrapper.run.start banner it qualifies, when Parallel mode degrades entirely to the serial path for the whole Run. Never emitted by a Run that fills, or could fill, a single Lane.
wrapper.parallel.degraded.scope: Run-scoped. It names a property of the Run's issue source, so it carries no contribution identity and no issue.
wrapper.parallel.degraded.not_a_fallback: Distinct from wrapper.parallel.serial_fallback, which reports one Iteration a Rolling-capable Run works because the Pool happens to hold no eligible Parallel-safe candidate. That one is per Iteration, is fixed by triage, and is counted; this one is per Run, is fixed by nothing inside the Run, and counts nothing.
wrapper.parallel.degraded.not_a_refusal: A distribution that cannot schedule Lanes at all MUST refuse a Lane cap above 1 at preflight. This is the other case: the manifest is truthful and the fallback works the same issues to the same outcome, stranding nothing.
wrapper.parallel.degraded.reported: The reason MUST reach the operator's own output, not only the Event stream: a degraded Run is byte-identical to a serial Run under a banner naming a Lane cap.
wrapper.parallel.degraded.capabilities: parallel_capabilities.parallel_mode stays true. The declaration is about the distribution; this record is about the Run.

contribution_identity.lane_id: The reusable Lane the contribution started in. It never changes, even after that Lane is refilled, so replay never needs a mutable Lane-to-issue lookup.
contribution_identity.legacy: Historical Wave traces carry lane_issue and no contribution identity. They remain readable and MUST NOT be reinterpreted as contributions.

calibration_identity.run_id_rule: A Calibration record MUST carry run_id null. A Trial is not an Iteration and a Calibration is not a Run: its Consumption is not a Run's Cost and its failures never reach the Strike counter.
calibration_identity.trial_id: Distinct for every Trial a Calibration runs, including two Trials of the same Proving task at different rungs, which the task pin alone could not separate.
calibration_identity.scope: Python-only, like the measured tier it serves (contract 14.1). The shell and PowerShell Orchestrators declare these literals and never emit them.

rolling_stream_cases.description: One Run that fills two Lanes, refills Lane 1 the moment its first contribution is admitted, parks a third finisher against the full H=2 Integration backlog and narrows for it, advances a patch Release line after closing its first Integration publication, recovers one contribution inside its private stage, latches Serial-required work, and passes over its last candidate with a Pickup skip that binds nothing.

highest verified Intelligence Index among the runnable configurations

rolling_stream_cases.description: A Parallel-mode Run whose tracker carries no parallel-safe issue. Every serial Iteration is a fallback, the reason is carried explicitly, and a Pressure signal this Run cannot observe stays null rather than being reported as zero.

The capability declares `false` and the card is an explicit `null` rather than an omitted key, so a reader can tell a Run that failed to resolve one from a producer that has no concept of one. `cost` stays `true` beside it: nothing derives a figure from the card, so an absent card costs no figure.
